clue.text: Doctor caught pinching journalist's wine

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between finger and thumb, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A doctor is caught stealing a reporter's bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor holds the journalist, and the catch follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux from the region of that name, so it is an example of wine.

clue.text: Like Eeyore's second expression of impatience

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
pish is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience

explanation.surface: Pooh's gloomy donkey friend is said to show a second sign of impatience.
explanation.walkthrough: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopish means dejected and listless, exactly the habitual mood of the downcast donkey in Milne's stories.

clue.text: Quiet old insider prepared to return to civilian employment

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up and put into new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A quiet former insider is ready to go back to an ordinary civilian job.
explanation.definitionFit: To derequisition is to release property or staff taken for military use, handing them back for ordinary peacetime purposes.

clue.text: Piece of meat — item regularly forming dish

parts.note: a cut is a portion of meat from a butcher

indicators.note: regularly means at a steady interval, so only every other letter of that word is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A slice of meat plus some other item makes up a dish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like food, but here it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is informal for a good-looking person, and a cutie is likewise an attractive, charming one.

clue.text: A woman's spells on a drug rejected in these parts

indicators.note: on in an across entry means placed after, so the spells come second
something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: A plus E, ecstasy, before turning
bouts are spells or periods of activity

explanation.surface: A woman's enchantments, cast while she is on a banned drug, are refused locally.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a common crossword abbreviation for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereabouts is an adverb meaning near this place, the same sense as the phrase about the local area.

clue.text: Passes first of workmen carrying a tool

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone hands over the foreman's kit, carrying a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsaw is a saw worked by one hand, a common carpentry tool.

clue.text: Go over again, about to surrender

parts.note: to capitulate is to give in

explanation.surface: Someone is about to give in, and so must go over things again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; split it, and 'about' is the first chunk while 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapitulate is to summarise or restate the main points, going back over them once more.

clue.text: Fax Mary starts off about affliction of the armpit

indicators.note: with their starts off, the two names lose their opening letters
about means surrounding, so the shortened names go around the next part

parts.note: an ill is a trouble or ailment

explanation.surface: Someone faxes Mary to report a complaint about an underarm ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Axillary is the anatomical adjective from axilla, the Latin medical term for the armpit.

clue.text: Like some cereal Oscar put away before noon

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to put away food is to eat it
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Oscar polished off his cereal before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaten means made of oats, as some breakfast cereals and porridges are.

clue.text: Like a Weill opera, costing very little once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Kurt Weill and Brecht's 1928 work
second meaning: priced at a small pre-decimal sum

explanation.walkthrough: Old British money had a coin worth three pennies; something costing that was cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Threepenny Opera is Weill's famous work, and a threepenny item cost three old pence, very little.

clue.text: Tactless remark primarily riling the chief electrician

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

explanation.surface: A clumsy comment annoys the head of the lighting crew.
explanation.definitionFit: On a film or TV set the gaffer is the head lighting technician in charge of the electrical department.

clue.text: Insistent a worker must shore up barrier

indicators.note: shoring something up supports it from either side, so the other letters flank the next word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a labourer must prop up the barricade.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone refusing to be moved, firmly insisting on a position.

clue.text: Completely safe dessert, one originally consumed by academic

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit pudding

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside, so the letter goes within the next word
originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

explanation.surface: A pudding is so safe that a professor eats it first.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit purée folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolproof means so simple or safe that nothing can go wrong, even in careless hands.

clue.text: Member of ruling family put up by Republican circle

parts.note: the letter shaped like a circle

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top, the other way round

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A prince is put up by a ring of Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a member of a monarch's family, the household that reigns.

clue.text: Intimates favour crooked man in scoop

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: all three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Close friends help out a dishonest man caught up in a press exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the man inside the scoop, but its letters belong to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Boon companions are close, convivial friends, the same idea as intimates used as a noun.

clue.text: Strait-laced Carthaginian woman making entry

indicators.note: making entry means going in, so the woman's name goes inside the other word

parts.note: Punic is the adjective for ancient Carthage

explanation.surface: A prim woman from ancient Carthage makes her entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Punic Wars were Rome's wars with Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritanic means puritanical, holding strict moral views, which is what strait-laced describes.

clue.text: Questioning politician on eg train or at sea

indicators.note: on in an across entry means placed after, so the politician goes second
at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A politician travelling by train or boat is quizzed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after: the politician follows the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrogatory is an adjective meaning asking questions, the same as questioning used adjectivally.

clue.text: What Parisian left among directions for follow-ups

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so these letters sit inside the others

parts.note: compass points south, east and south

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's left asks what the directions are for the follow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequels are works or events that follow on from earlier ones, which is what follow-ups are.

clue.text: Friend eager to carry a new covered litter

indicators.note: to carry is to hold inside, so the friend and eager words enclose the rest

explanation.surface: A keen friend offers to carry a new covered stretcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A palankeen, or palanquin, is an enclosed seat carried on poles, a covered litter used in Asia.

clue.text: Horrify a reindeer herder going west

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the Lapps, or Sami, herd reindeer in northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A reindeer keeper heading off west fills someone with horror.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or dismay someone deeply, the same as to horrify.

clue.text: How it dries rice out? That's novel

indicators.note: out here means disordered, put out of place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: all four words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks how rice dries out, and is told that is new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but it is the noun: a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's 1959 memoir-style novel of a Cotswold village childhood.

clue.text: Free former con briefly at end of sentence

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
end of asks for only the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A former convict is released briefly at the end of his prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a convict, which fits 'sentence', but it is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free someone or something from a difficulty or entanglement.

clue.text: Vestment certain to incorporate new clip

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so one word holds the other
new means made over afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church robe is sure to need a new fastening clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplice is a loose white linen garment worn over a cassock by clergy and choristers, a vestment.

clue.text: Pole with old hat in distant settlement

parts.note: old hat means outdated, out of fashion

explanation.surface: A Polish man wearing an old hat lives somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' with a capital looks like a Polish person; it is a wooden post. 'With' puts the pieces side by side, read in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small remote settlement or station far from the main centre.

clue.text: Practical sciences only the GOC deployed

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and arranged, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: all three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Only the general officer commanding has applied science at his disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: GOC is the army abbreviation for General Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology is the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, the practical sciences.

clue.text: Stressed computer studies woman with daughter touring islands

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the woman's name goes around the islands

explanation.surface: A tense computing student travels the islands with her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stressed' looks like anxious; it means emphasised, as italic type does.
explanation.definitionFit: Italicised text is set in sloping type, the usual way of emphasising words in print.

clue.text: Son finally abandons water-starved sheep in fairish number

indicators.note: abandons means leaves out, so that letter is dropped from the next word

parts.note: the fold is a flock of sheep, or its pen

explanation.surface: A son at last leaves the thirsty flock, which numbers a fair few.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirtyfold means thirty times over, a multiplier giving a fairly large number.

clue.text: Experience efficient estate manager's sense of wellbeing

parts.note: good at a job means efficient
in Scotland a factor manages a landed estate

explanation.surface: A capable estate manager has a sense of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: The feel-good factor is a widespread sense of optimism and contentment, especially about the economy.

clue.text: Crossing ocean it finally moved quickly, having particular sound

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before
having its sound means a word spelt differently but heard the same

explanation.surface: A ship finally sped across the sea, making a distinctive noise.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: SPECIFIC is said almost like S-PACIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpacific means across the Pacific, so it describes crossing that ocean.

clue.text: Nagging civilian in garrison principally restricting husband

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the civilian word encloses the husband

parts.note: civvy is slang for a civilian

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, first, so only the opening letter of that word is kept

explanation.surface: A nagging civilian in the barracks keeps her husband on a tight leash.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivvying means harassing or urging someone on persistently, which is what nagging is.

clue.text: Woollen items knight placed among gear on river

indicators.note: on in a down entry means placed above, so the gear comes before the river
placed among means set within, so the knight goes inside the gear

parts.note: N is the knight in chess notation
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A knight packs woollens among his kit beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is the collective name for knitted garments such as jumpers, typically woollen.

clue.text: Italian fellow's regularly alluring air

indicators.note: regularly means at a steady interval, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: An Italian man has a seductive manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi is a common Italian man's name, the equivalent of Louis.

clue.text: Confuse viewpoint of otolaryngologists?

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: The specialists' perspective is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: Otolaryngologists are ear, nose and throat doctors, known as ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to twist into a tangle or muddle, so it can mean to confuse.

clue.text: One of Mitford's aristos accepting suggestion for psalm

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the aristocrat words enclose the suggestion

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
the Hons are the aristocratic children in Nancy Mitford's novels

explanation.surface: A Mitford aristocrat takes up a hint about choosing a psalm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hon is short for Honourable, the courtesy title of a peer's children, central to Mitford's world.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a psalm or hymn sung in alternating parts by two choirs.

clue.text: Greek character with house worked in mythic Asian port

indicators.note: worked means shaped and processed, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Greek hero and his house appear in a legendary port of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing things inside; its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon, is Vietnam's largest city and a major river port.

clue.text: Artist in Irish county composed airs outside eastern inn

indicators.note: in means inside, so the artist sits within the county
outside means on the exterior, so the shuffled tunes wrap around the compass letter

parts.note: Cavan is a county in Ireland

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A painter in Ireland composes tunes about the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' places the shuffled airs around the E, though that only fixes letters already in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanserai is a roadside inn with a courtyard where caravans rested in the Middle East and Asia.

clue.text: Study dance, providing fee for postponement

parts.note: to con is to study or learn

explanation.surface: Learning a dance earns a fee for being put off.
explanation.walkthrough: Contango is an old London Stock Exchange term.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango was the charge paid by a buyer to defer settlement of a share purchase to the next account.

clue.text: Detached Roman statesman with animals from the east

indicators.note: coming from the east in an across entry means reading right to left

explanation.surface: An aloof Roman politician arrives with beasts from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detached' looks like aloof; in music it means short and separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is the musical term for notes played sharply detached from one another.

clue.text: Outspoken woman receiving military commander

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the woman's name holds the commander

explanation.surface: A forthright woman welcomes an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal means expressing opinions freely and forcefully, which an outspoken person does.

clue.text: Peevish type giving mongrel a common dog's name

parts.note: Patch is a typical name for a dog

explanation.surface: A grumpy owner gives his mixed-breed dog an ordinary name.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an informal word for a bad-tempered, irritable person.

clue.text: Upright rider's second woman at frontier, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means what is said out loud, so the spelling may differ

explanation.surface: A rider's second wife waits at the frontier, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A skateboarder rides a board standing up, so he is a rider who stays upright.

clue.text: One leaving Francis's place beat rear of flippant aide

indicators.note: one leaving means the letter for one goes out of the town's name

parts.note: St Francis came from Assisi in Italy
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: rear of asks for only the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A flippant helper leaves the Franciscan town after a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who helps another in their work, which is what an aide does.

clue.text: Saw about taking to the water and making merry

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: sailing is going out on the water

explanation.surface: A sailor spotted people taking to the water and celebrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is drinking and carousing in festive celebration, especially at Christmas, so it means making merry.

clue.text: Society family not so devoid of cover

explanation.surface: A high-society family is not so well protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinless means having no skin, the outer covering of a sausage, fruit or body.

clue.text: Cleft stick girl's found by river at Pontypridd

parts.note: Di's, a girl's name with the possessive
the Taff flows through Pontypridd in South Wales

explanation.surface: A girl's forked stick is discovered beside a Welsh river.
explanation.definitionFit: A distaff is the cleft staff on which wool or flax was held for spinning by hand.

clue.text: One flying aircraft at first by way of rocky peak

indicators.note: at first means at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A pilot's aircraft passes over a craggy summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies an aircraft.

clue.text: Mount further industrial action, ringing pub to agree on terms

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the action phrase surrounds the pub

explanation.surface: Unions stage another walkout, phoning the pub to settle a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a bargain is to reach an agreement over the terms of a deal.

clue.text: Current board suitable for representing on stage

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: The present board decides what is fit to perform in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Actable describes a play or part that can be acted effectively in performance.

clue.text: Take up residence in N Yorks town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make a home somewhere
second meaning: a market town in the Yorkshire Dales

explanation.surface: Someone moves to live in a North Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in North Yorkshire, on the Settle to Carlisle railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make a permanent home, and Settle is also the name of a Dales town.

clue.text: Singers in Cuba's side-streets

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the words

explanation.surface: Musicians perform in the back streets of Havana.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassi is the Italian plural of basso, singers with the lowest male voices.

clue.text: High-ranking Muslim woman, say, taken in by tramp

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the example word goes within the tramp

parts.note: eg means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: A noblewoman, say, is fooled by a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Begum is a title for a Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia.

clue.text: Gangster's way to enter parts of builders' course

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the way goes within the gangster's name

explanation.surface: A gangster's route leads him into a building course.
explanation.walkthrough: A course in building is a row of bricks or stones; the top one is the capping layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Capstones are the stones forming the top course of a wall, a part of the masonry.

clue.text: Leaving hospital, get excited and sing

indicators.note: leaving means going out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to thrill is to get excited
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient discharged from hospital is so excited she bursts into song.
explanation.definitionFit: To trill is to sing or warble with a quavering, rapidly alternating sound.

clue.text: Foot of giant bird encountered in the east

indicators.note: encountered in means met inside, so the bird sits within the last words

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: The foot of a giant bird is spotted in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks anatomical, fitting the bird; it is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed then one unstressed syllable.

clue.text: Work on island with hesitation, producing narcotic drug

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Labour on an island, punctuated by hesitation, yields a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the narcotic made from the dried latex of the opium poppy.

clue.text: Slow mover gets into a riot, carelessly

indicators.note: done carelessly, things end up out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all four words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A slow walker blunders into a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant tortoises, of the Galápagos and Aldabra, are famously slow-moving reptiles.

clue.text: Talmudic scholar's chatter about rejection of wrongdoing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatter word goes around the rest

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter on

indicators.note: a rejection sends something back, so the word runs the other way

explanation.surface: A rabbinical scholar talks about refusing to do wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbinist is an adherent or student of the Talmud and the teachings of the rabbis.

clue.text: Fully developed type demanding change of leader

indicators.note: a change of leader means the opening letter is swapped for another

explanation.surface: A grown-up character insists on a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The substitute first letter is not clued; the definition alone fixes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mature means fully grown or ripened, having reached complete development.

clue.text: Uncultivated Greek character given inventory in English

explanation.surface: A boorish Greek is handed a stock list written in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine person is hostile or indifferent to art and culture, so uncultivated in taste.

clue.text: Part of spring attached to 50% of beds, perhaps

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half, so only the first half of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first two of four letters

explanation.surface: Spring flowers are attached to half the flowerbeds, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe is an adverb meaning possibly, the same as perhaps.
